requests.brief: New sim, to be built by sim-builder as our own bundle; no PhET code, art or layout (PhET sims are CC BY-NC 4.0). Concept: phy.laws-of-motion.friction.core.static-kinetic-friction. Learning goal: tilt a plank with a block on it and see that static friction is self-adjusting: it equals mg sin(theta) while the block stays at rest, up to the limit mu_s N with N = mg cos(theta); once tan(theta) exceeds mu_s the block slides and the friction drops to the kinetic value mu_k N. Model: N = m g cos(theta); at rest f = m g sin(theta) while m g sin(theta) <= mu_s N; sliding f = mu_k N and a = g (sin(theta) - mu_k cos(theta)). Params: mass (kg, 0.5 to 10, default 2), mu_s (0 to 1, default 0.5), mu_k (0 to mu_s, default 0.4), angle (degrees, 0 to 60, default 0), g (m/s^2, default 9.8). Controls: slider for angle, sliders for mass, mu_s and mu_k, reset. The sim draws force arrows for weight, normal force and friction with text labels (not colour alone). Background art, if any, comes from visual-director, not drawn in the sim. Readouts the card reads: friction (N), normal_force (N), angle (degrees). Card tasks with mass 2, mu_s 0.5, g 9.8: friction at 15 degrees 5.07 N; friction at 20 degrees 6.70 N; slip angle 26.6 degrees. Model tests: these values, and NCERT Example 4.8 (block starts to slide at 15 degrees, so mu_s = tan 15 = 0.27). Reduced motion: no sliding animation; show the end state and the readouts at once.
